title: Each test file a lane touches runs on Windows before the batch
why: Lane lint runs on Linux only, and #1543's trigger runs the Windows shards only when guard files change. So a Windows-only red in a skill test reaches the batch run, drops the lane and costs a full rebuild. Incident: #1472 (map import aliases), T11b in skills/plain-english-map/tests/fact-lines.test.mjs line 817, dropped from batch 63 #1782 at 23:12 CST Nov 7 (runner 8; coordinator, 23:21 CST).
note: Fix: #1543's trigger, or lane lint, runs on Windows every test file a lane touches. Not folded into step guard-pr-runs-windows-shards: its PR #1543 is open and scoped to guard diffs, and widening it mid-review restarts its review. Build on #1543's trigger after it merges, or stack on it. A queue fix under the item 384 hold. Slug from the coordinator; title by triage. 23:22 CST: lane session_013NEJL4HeTtQTFg5s9G62RY, stacked on #1543. 23:30 CST: the lane waits on owner page item 400 windows-run-per-lane (a draft-only Windows job, a lane-dispatched run, or keep today). Incident 2, 23:36 CST: #1487's caseM17 fails only on shell-macos, so batch #1783 was rebuilt as #1794. The same gap covers macOS: the per-lane job runs touched tests on macOS too where a macOS job exists. Item 400 now says so (coordinator). Owner item 400 a (06:08 CST Nov 8): checks.yml gets one job that runs on a draft PR, on Windows and on macOS where a macOS job exists, and runs only the test files the lane changed. Home: decision draft-until-reviewed. Departure the lane reported (06:16 CST Nov 8): the job goes in its own workflow file, .github/workflows/lane-touched-tests.yml, not checks.yml, because inside checks.yml it would sit off all-jobs-passed and ci-hygiene audit item 2 flags that; tests checks.yml runs on one OS only (.ps1, ios-ship) run only there or are listed by name. Done: .github/workflows/lane-touched-tests.yml on main (3bd877a70, 1f50f00e4, 50242b8c0); #1543 and #1487 are stale cites (triage reader agent, Explore Sonnet audit, read of origin/main 0e6509a96, 06:03 CST Nov 10).
